question.problem: A company manufactures three types of cars. Of the car population, $40%$ are model ${C}_{1},$  $35%$ are model ${C}_{2},$ and the remaining cars are model ${C}_{3}.$ If $6%$ of the model ${C}_{1},$ $4%$ of the model  ${C}_{2},$ and $2%$ of the model ${C}_{3}$ cars break down during the first year, what is the probability that a randomly selected car will break down during the first year?
question.worked_solution:
Let $B$ be the event that a randomly selected car breaks down during the first year, and 

- let ${C}_{1}$ be the event that the car is of model ${C}_{1},$

- let ${C}_{2}$ be the event that the car is of model ${C}_{2},$

- let ${C}_{3}$ be the event that the car is of model ${C}_{3}.$

Then the disjoint union ${C}_{1}⊔{C}_{2}⊔{C}_{3}$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected car will break down during the first year, we can use the law of total probability: 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(B) & =P(B\cap {C}_{1})+P(B\cap {C}_{2})+P(B\cap {C}_{3}) \\  & =P(B|{C}_{1})P({C}_{1})+P(B|{C}_{2})P({C}_{2})+P(B|{C}_{3})P({C}_{3})\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since $40%$ of the cars produced by the company are model ${C}_{1},$ and $50%$ are model ${C}_{2},$  the model ${C}_{3}$ cars make up the remaining

$$
100%-(40%+35%)=25%.
$$

As a result, we have

$$
P({C}_{1})=0.4,\,P({C}_{2})=0.35,\,P({C}_{3})=0.25.
$$

- Since $6%$ of the cars of model ${C}_{1},$ $4%$ of those of model  ${C}_{2},$ and $2%$ of the cars of model ${C}_{3}$ break down during the first year, we have

$$
P(B|{C}_{1})=0.06,\,P(B|{C}_{2})=0.04,\,P(B|{C}_{3})=0.02.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected car breaks down during the first year is 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(B) & =P(B|{C}_{1})P({C}_{1})+P(B|{C}_{2})P({C}_{2})+P(B|{C}_{3})P({C}_{3}) \\  & =(0.06)(0.4)+(0.04)(0.35)+(0.02)(0.25) \\  & =0.024+0.014+0.005 \\  & =0.043.\end{aligned}
$$
